Title: Next-Generation Metabolic Models: From Multi-Constraint Integration to AI-Driven Whole-Cell Kinetic Simulation
Summary: Reviews next-generation metabolic models from multi-constraint integration to AI-driven whole-cell kinetic simulation, including flux balance analysis and metabolic pathway analysis.

Title: DigiPhen: a new paradigm for building predictive models of biological systems
Summary: Presents DigiPhen, a digital phenome platform that combines experimental, analytical, and modeling workflows to build multi-scale predictive models of microbial and plant phenotypes.

Title: PEtab SciML: an exchange format for specifying and training dynamic scientific machine learning models
Summary: Introduces PEtab SciML, an exchange format and tooling for specifying and jointly training mechanistic ODE and machine-learning components in dynamic scientific machine-learning models.

Title: A Structural Theory of Admissible Transitions in Biological Reaction Networks
Summary: Introduces admissible transitions, a kinetics-independent structural criterion for feasible changes between species configurations in biological reaction networks.

Title: Application and progress of synthetic biology technology in amino acid production
Summary: Reviews synthetic biology strategies for amino acid production, covering metabolic pathway design, genetic circuits, dynamic regulation, and high-throughput screening.

Title: Metabolic engineering of Rhodococcus aromaticivorans RHA1 for muconic acid production from lignin
Summary: Engineers Rhodococcus aromaticivorans RHA1 to convert kraft lignin-derived aromatics (vanillin, vanillate, and acetovanillone) to muconic acid at 97% molar yield.

Title: Improving acetate metabolism of P. putida KT2440 by evolutionary and rational engineering
Summary: Combines rational overexpression of acetyl-CoA synthetase with adaptive laboratory evolution to improve Pseudomonas putida KT2440 growth and HAA production on acetate.

Title: Engineering Escherichia coli to modulate hydrogen sulfide levels using insights from intestinal sulfur metabolism
Summary: Engineers Escherichia coli strains to produce or consume hydrogen sulfide in specific intestinal regions by incorporating local metabolic environment into the design.

Title: Engineering Synthetic Membraneless Organelles Towards Efficient Hydrogen Production in Escherichia coli
Summary: Engineers synthetic membraneless organelles in Escherichia coli to compartmentalize hydrogenase activity toward more efficient hydrogen production.

Title: Engineering Microbial Consortia for Coordinated Control of Metabolic Roles and Electron Flows in Dark-Fermentative Hydrogen Production
Summary: Reviews microbial consortium engineering to coordinate metabolic roles and electron flows for more selective and stable dark-fermentative hydrogen production.
